raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
### Motivation

Fixes #34482.

`--vae-tiling` was silently ignored for Sana models: the `AutoencoderDC` wrapper
does not proxy `enable_tiling` to the inner diffusers model, so the call raised
`AttributeError`, which (at the time this PR was opened) was swallowed by a bare
`except` in `DecodingStage`. On 8GB GPUs this turns a would-be-successful
generation into a fatal OOM after the full denoising loop has already run. See
the issue for the root-cause chain.

### Modifications

- `runtime/models/vaes/autoencoder_dc.py`: proxy `enable_tiling` /
  `disable_tiling` to the inner diffusers `AutoencoderDC`, which already
  implements them. `enable_tiling` is a no-op (with `warning_once`) when
  spatial-shard parallel decode is installed on this wrapper, since diffusers'
  `tiled_decode` running per-rank inside a height-sharded decoder breaks the
  halo exchange (mismatched collective rounds / wrong neighbours).
- `configs/models/vaes/sana.py`, `configs/pipeline_configs/sana.py`: update
  the two comments that claimed DC-AE tiling is unsupported.
- `test/unit/test_autoencoder_dc.py`: CPU-only unit test asserting the proxy
  forwards to the inner model and that the spatial-shard guard is a no-op.

### Scope / decisions

- **Default unchanged.** `SanaPipelineConfig.vae_tiling` stays `False`; tiling
  is opt-in via `--vae-tiling`. DC-AE is a 32x-compression autoencoder and
  tile seam quality / the benefit of diffusers' default 512 tile have not been
  validated, so a default flip does not belong in a bugfix.
- **`decoding.py` is no longer touched.** The v1 of this PR also replaced the
  bare `except` around `enable_tiling()` with a warning; main has since fixed
  that call site independently (specific `AttributeError` handling + warning),
  so that change is dropped here and the PR is now purely the wrapper-side fix.

### Test / Verification

- Before: `sglang generate --model-path Efficient-Large-Model/Sana_600M_512px_diffusers
  --prompt "..." --save-output --vae-tiling` — fatal OOM in `DecodingStage` on
  RTX 4070 Laptop 8GB (3/3 runs). Note: with DC-AE's 32x compression, tiling
  only engages at ≥1024x1024 (512x512 gives a 16x16 latent == `tile_latent_min`).
- After: same command (1024x1024) succeeds end-to-end; output image correct.
  This PR changes correctness (OOM → success), not performance; timings are
  not reported.
- `pytest python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_autoencoder_dc.py` passes.
- pre-commit clean.

Thanks for the thorough review — addressed in the latest push:

1. Spatial-shard + tiling: `enable_tiling` is now a no-op with `warning_once`
   when `_spatial_parallel_decode_enabled` is set, plus a unit test for it.
   Went with the no-op rather than `disable_spatial_parallel_decode()` to keep
   the change local to the wrapper; happy to switch if you'd prefer the
   qwenimage pattern.
2. Both stale comments (`configs/models/vaes/sana.py`,
   `configs/pipeline_configs/sana.py`) updated; added the `_ensure_inner_model`
   note you suggested.
3. Default: keeping `vae_tiling=False`, now stated explicitly in the
   description and in the config comment.
4. Scope: the `decoding.py` warning change is dropped from this PR — main has
   since fixed that call site with specific `AttributeError` handling, so after
   rebase this PR is purely the wrapper-side proxy fix (plus guard, comments,
   test). Noted in the description.

The `tile_latent_min` observation is very useful — forwarding tile geometry
from the config looks like a natural follow-up for the 8GB case; I'll open an
issue for it.

All review feedback from @triple-mu has been addressed in a4c632a
(spatial-shard mutual-exclusion guard, stale config comments,
default-decision documentation). The DecodingStage side landed
independently in #35353, so this PR now only carries the AutoencoderDC
wrapper side — 4 files, no overlap with main, merges cleanly.
@mickqian since you just touched this area in #35353, could you
trigger run-ci / take a look when you get a chance?

## Local verification (amacs-dev · RTX 3050 sm86)

Checked against current `main` vs this PR head:

- `main` `AutoencoderDC` has `enable_tiling`: **No** (bug still present)
- This PR adds `enable_tiling` / `disable_tiling`: **Yes**
- Unit contract: forward kwargs to inner model: **PASS**
- Spatial-shard decode => tiling noop: **PASS**
- `main`-like wrapper without method => `AttributeError`: **PASS** (matches decoding.py warn path)

So the fix still looks correct and necessary on today's main. Happy to help if you need a rebase / re-trigger `run-ci` — call-gate previously failed on missing `run-ci-extra`, and several AMD multimodal jobs were red.

Thanks @quantz8a for the independent verification on sm86!

@mickqian @BBuf — status summary for merge: both required checks (`lint`, `pr-test-finish`) are green, as are all NVIDIA multimodal-gen suites. The remaining red jobs are unrelated to this PR: the AMD multimodal jobs have also failed on the last 5 `main` runs (09-01 → 09-09), and the NPU/XPU failures are timeouts/cancellations. The existing approval is from @triple-mu, who per GitHub's CODEOWNERS check doesn't have write access, so it doesn't count toward merge. Could one of you take a look and approve when you get a chance? No conflicts with current `main`.

>    note you suggested.
> 3. Default: keeping `vae_tiling=False`, now stated explicitly in the
>    description and in the config comment.
> 4. Scope: the `decoding.py` warning change is dropped from this PR — main has
>    since fixed that call site with specific `AttributeError` handling, so after
>    rebase this PR is purely the wrapper-side proxy fix (plus guard, comments,
>    test). Noted in the description.
> 
> The `tile_latent_min` observation is very useful — forwarding tile geometry from the config looks like a natural follow-up for the 8GB case; I'll open an issue for it.

The tiling guard works, but the earlier load-order assumption no longer holds at this head. `VAELoader` calls `state_dict()` before loading weights, so the existing early return in `_ensure_inner_model()` discards the checkpoint. This also reproduces on the base. Could you restore checkpoint weights when the inner model already exists and add a native-loader regression before considering Sana output correctness cleared?

The root cause analysis is accurate, and the change is appropriately minimal with no impact on default behaviour (the pipeline config is only overridden when `--vae-tiling` is passed explicitly). Proxying to the inner model is the right approach. A few things to address before merge:

**1. Once tiling actually takes effect, its combination with spatial-shard parallel decode becomes live** (previously inert, because `enable_tiling` raised and the exception was swallowed). See the inline comment.

**2. Two comments no longer match the code -- please update them as well** (neither file is touched by this PR):
- `configs/models/vaes/sana.py:29-30`
- `configs/pipeline_configs/sana.py:52`

These are comment-only issues with no runtime contradiction: `SanaVAEConfig.use_tiling` is never read for this VAE; the actual switch is `pipeline_config.vae_tiling`.

**3. Please settle the default value of `SanaPipelineConfig.vae_tiling` in this PR.** My suggestion is to keep it `False`: DC-AE is a 32x-compression autoencoder, and both the tile seam quality and the real benefit of the default 512 tile need to be validated separately. Changing the default rendering behaviour for every Sana user inside a bugfix is not ideal. If the decision is to keep it as is, please state that explicitly rather than leaving it open.

**4. Please note the scope of the fix in the description.** The same bare `except` still exists at `image_encoding.py:615/928`, `realtime/vae.py:152`, `mova.py:983` and `ltx_2/decoding_av.py:87`, and `encoding.py:111` has no `try` at all. Fixing only the decoding path is reasonable -- none of the others is reachable for `AutoencoderDC` -- but a sentence in the description would keep this from reading as an oversight.

For reference, and not something to handle in this PR: `enable_tiling()` is called without arguments, so diffusers' default 512 sample tile applies. With DC-AE's 32x compression a 512x512 output has a 16x16 latent, which equals `tile_latent_min`, so tiling does not actually engage until 1024x1024. The ~386MB non-fatal allocator retries you reported in the issue are likely related to the tile being large; if you want to push the 8GB case further, forwarding the tile geometry from the config would be a reasonable follow-up.

Consider making this a no-op (with a warning) when `self._spatial_parallel_decode_enabled` is true, or documenting that the two features cannot be enabled together.

With spatial-shard decode installed, `decode()` splits the latent by height via `tensor_split` and the convolutions are replaced by `SpatialParallelConv2d`, which performs halo exchanges. After this PR, diffusers' `tiled_decode` runs tile by tile *inside* each rank's shard, so the number of collective rounds becomes a function of each rank's shard height. For example, with a latent height of 128 across 3 ranks, `tensor_split` gives 43/43/42: ranks 0 and 1 run 4 tile iterations while rank 2 runs 3, which hangs. With equal shard heights there is no hang, but each rank's tiles map to different global rows, so the halo neighbours are wrong and the bottom band of each shard is corrupted.

Triggering this requires explicitly passing `--vae-config.parallel-decode-mode spatial_shard`, so the reachability is narrow and I would not treat it as blocking. `autoencoder_kl_qwenimage.py:1102` and `hunyuanvae.py:950` guard exactly this combination with `with disable_spatial_parallel_decode():` and may be a useful reference.

     use_tiling: bool = False

@@ -48,7 +48,10 @@ class SanaPipelineConfig(SpatialImagePipelineConfig):
     should_use_guidance: bool = False
     enable_autocast: bool = False
 
-    # DC-AE does not support tiling or SP VAE decode yet.
+    # Tiled decode is supported (--vae-tiling) but kept off by default: DC-AE
+    # is a 32x-compression autoencoder and tile seam quality / the benefit of
+    # diffusers' default 512 tile have not been validated. SP VAE decode is
+    # not supported.
     vae_tiling: bool = False
     vae_sp: bool = False

@@ -136,6 +136,26 @@ def device(self):
             return next(self._inner_model.parameters()).device
         return torch.device("cpu")
 
+    def enable_tiling(self, *args, **kwargs):
+        # Proxy to the inner diffusers model, which already implements tiled
+        # decode; this wrapper just didn't forward the call before.
+        self._ensure_inner_model()
+        if self._spatial_parallel_decode_enabled:
+            # Tiling runs diffusers' tiled_decode independently inside each
+            # rank's height shard, which breaks the halo exchange of the
+            # spatially sharded decoder (mismatched collective rounds / wrong
+            # neighbours). Keep the two mutually exclusive.
+            logger.warning_once(
+                "AutoencoderDC: --vae-tiling is ignored because spatial-shard "
+                "parallel decode is enabled; the two cannot be combined."
+            )
+            return
+        self._inner_model.enable_tiling(*args, **kwargs)
+
+    def disable_tiling(self):
+        self._ensure_inner_model()
+        self._inner_model.disable_tiling()
+
     @cached_vae_encode
     def encode(self, x: torch.Tensor, **kwargs):
         self._ensure_inner_model()

@@ -0,0 +1,44 @@
+import unittest
+
+from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.models.vaes.autoencoder_dc import AutoencoderDC
+
+
+class _FakeInnerModel:
+    def __init__(self):
+        self.tiling_enabled = False
+        self.enable_tiling_kwargs = None
+
+    def enable_tiling(self, **kwargs):
+        self.tiling_enabled = True
+        self.enable_tiling_kwargs = kwargs
+
+    def disable_tiling(self):
+        self.tiling_enabled = False
+
+
+class TestAutoencoderDCTiling(unittest.TestCase):
+    def setUp(self) -> None:
+        # Once _inner_model is set, _ensure_inner_model() is a no-op, so no
+        # real diffusers model is constructed.
+        self.wrapper = AutoencoderDC()
+        self.fake_inner = _FakeInnerModel()
+        self.wrapper._inner_model = self.fake_inner
+
+    def test_tiling_calls_forward_to_inner_model(self) -> None:
+        self.wrapper.enable_tiling(tile_sample_min_height=512)
+        self.assertTrue(self.fake_inner.tiling_enabled)
+        self.assertEqual(
+            self.fake_inner.enable_tiling_kwargs, {"tile_sample_min_height": 512}
+        )
+
+        self.wrapper.disable_tiling()
+        self.assertFalse(self.fake_inner.tiling_enabled)
+
+    def test_enable_tiling_is_noop_with_spatial_shard_decode(self) -> None:
+        self.wrapper._spatial_parallel_decode_enabled = True
+        self.wrapper.enable_tiling()
+        self.assertFalse(self.fake_inner.tiling_enabled)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

> 
> The `tile_latent_min` observation is very useful — forwarding tile geometry from the config looks like a natural follow-up for the 8GB case; I'll open an issue for it.

The tiling guard works, but the earlier load-order assumption no longer holds at this head. `VAELoader` calls `state_dict()` before loading weights, so the existing early return in `_ensure_inner_model()` discards the checkpoint. reviews.body:
The root cause analysis is accurate, and the change is appropriately minimal with no impact on default behaviour (the pipeline config is only overridden when `--vae-tiling` is passed explicitly). Proxying to the inner model is the right approach. A few things to address before merge:

**1. Once tiling actually takes effect, its combination with spatial-shard parallel decode becomes live** (previously inert, because `enable_tiling` raised and the exception was swallowed). See the inline comment.

**2. Two comments no longer match the code -- please update them as well** (neither file is touched by this PR):
- `configs/models/vaes/sana.py:29-30`
- `configs/pipeline_configs/sana.py:52`

These are comment-only issues with no runtime contradiction: `SanaVAEConfig.use_tiling` is never read for this VAE; the actual switch is `pipeline_config.vae_tiling`.

**3. Please settle the default value of `SanaPipelineConfig.vae_tiling` in this PR.** My suggestion is to keep it `False`: DC-AE is a 32x-compression autoencoder, and both the tile seam quality and the real benefit of the default 512 tile need to be validated separately. Changing the default rendering behaviour for every Sana user inside a bugfix is not ideal. If the decision is to keep it as is, please state that explicitly rather than leaving it open.

**4. Please note the scope of the fix in the description.** The same bare `except` still exists at `image_encoding.py:615/928`, `realtime/vae.py:152`, `mova.py:983` and `ltx_2/decoding_av.py:87`, and `encoding.py:111` has no `try` at all. Fixing only the decoding path is reasonable -- none of the others is reachable for `AutoencoderDC` -- but a sentence in the description would keep this from reading as an oversight.

For reference, and not something to handle in this PR: `enable_tiling()` is called without arguments, so diffusers' default 512 sample tile applies. With DC-AE's 32x compression a 512x512 output has a 16x16 latent, which equals `tile_latent_min`, so tiling does not actually engage until 1024x1024. The ~386MB non-fatal allocator retries you reported in the issue are likely related to the tile being large; if you want to push the 8GB case further, forwarding the tile geometry from the config would be a reasonable follow-up.
